markdown_report:
**Prioritize a scoring-path audit before changing GRU4Rec’s memory mechanism.** At 10% progress, resolving the failed execution checks offers the clearest next experiment.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) All four categories fail final-feature consistency, with maximum discrepancies of 0.000163–0.000633. These measurements establish an unresolved execution difference, not its cause. (2) Reported valid-feature and candidate-score discrepancies are zero despite final-feature differences. Intermediate tensors and scoring dependence therefore need examination before attributing failures to recurrent padding. (3) Sampled training margins are positive, while temporal metrics remain unavailable. Neither result establishes recent-context utility or validation improvement.

**Insights from related work.** (1) PyTorch documents that GRU biases and recurrence can update states on zero inputs [1]. Padding invariance is therefore appropriate only when the trained implementation skips padding transitions. (2) PyTorch also documents numerical differences between batched and individual computations [2]. Repetition and batch transformations should distinguish numerical variation from indexing or execution defects. (3) Model-level metamorphic testing motivates tracing equivalent executions through intermediate layers [3]. Here, deliberately changing selected features can additionally establish whether the scoring hook consumes them.

**Framework and directions.** Organize evidence into three linked directions: execution equivalence, scoring-path dependence, and behavioral sensitivity. Their respective controls are identical-history batch transformations, controlled feature interventions, and final-item-fixed history perturbations; their outputs are tensor discrepancies, score changes, and paired ranking changes. Behavioral interpretation follows execution verification.

| Atomic idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Execution-to-score trace [1–3] | 4: focused integration; established testing methods | 8: resolves a blocking ambiguity; no direct accuracy gain | 3: frozen-model replay; predictor parity requires care |
| Final-item-fixed shuffle [1–2] | 4: isolates earlier order; familiar perturbation | 7: guides memory experiments; in-sample distribution shift limits inference | 3: existing hooks; paired uncertainty needs care |
| Hidden-state restoration [4] | 6: transfers patching to GRU recommendation; established intervention | 7: distinguishes attenuation from readout sensitivity; donor choice affects conclusions | 6: one frozen model; recurrent replay requires instrumentation |

**Selected algorithm: execution-to-score trace.** Cache identical nonempty histories and fixed candidates. Compare repeated, singleton, duplicated, permuted, and partitioned batches, restoring row order. Trace embeddings, recurrent outputs, the maximum-nonzero-position feature, output projection, and raw candidate scores through ModelView and the emitted predictor. Include empty-history handling separately.

For each mismatch, report absolute and relative errors, tolerance violations, candidate-score changes, and top-10 changes. Inject a deterministic feature displacement and compare score responses against the actual scoring equation; an unchanged response requires investigation, not an automatic defect verdict. Use stricter precision only as a diagnostic reference. Do not relax tolerances merely to unlock temporal results.

Preserve the diagnostic API, model mode, RNG states, and existing metrics. Keep one GRU4Rec checkpoint per category and all benchmark settings fixed. Any proven semantic correction requires matching training and predictor changes; official macro validation HR@10 remains the sole selection criterion.

idea.description: Trace identical histories from GRU4Rec embeddings through final-state selection and candidate scoring to resolve the observed final-feature discrepancies before interpreting temporal interventions.
idea.motivation: All four execution checks fail, yet reported candidate-score differences are zero. This leaves padding behavior, numerical variation, readout selection, and scoring-path dependence unresolved; the supplied evidence does not justify a recency architecture change.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve existing embedding and margin probes. Use the actual view.model and compatible item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). Run bounded replay in evaluation/inference mode, restoring prior mode and RNG states. Gather the maximum nonzero position for left-padded histories, never count-1; handle empty histories separately. Compare raw tensors before formatting or rounding, and record each comparison's input identity, shape, dtype, denominator, tolerance violations, and error location. Separate identical-input execution transformations from changed-padding comparisons: the latter are equivalence tests only if trained recurrence skips padding transitions. Test feature-to-score dependence against the actual projection, embeddings, and trained biases; use analytic displacement predictions only where the readout is linear. Compare ModelView with emitted-predictor scores under identical histories and candidates without altering the evaluator. Unresolved checks leave affected temporal metrics null with reasons. Preserve all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution. Each category retains exactly one independently trained GRU4Rec model; no fusion or checkpoint averaging. If a proven correction changes model semantics, retrain consistently and update the embedded predictor writer and checkpoint loader together. Use no hidden test data or unavailable metadata. Record diagnostic runtime against the shared budget; claim no validation gain before host measurement.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save model mode and RNG states
    try:
        set actual model to eval; enter inference_mode
        retain existing embedding and sampled-margin measurements
        cache bounded histories and fixed candidate IDs
        for execution in [repeat, singleton, duplicate, permute, partition]:
            replay identical histories; restore original row order
            trace embeddings, recurrent features, selected final features,
                  output projections and raw candidate scores where accessible
            compare corresponding tensors and report explicit tolerances
        separately audit empty rows and padding semantics
        for cached nonempty history:
            h = features at maximum nonzero sequence position
            delta = deterministic bounded feature displacement
            compare score(h + delta, candidates) with score(h, candidates)
            check response against the actual scoring equation
        compare ModelView scores with emitted-predictor scores
        if execution equivalence or scoring dependence remains unresolved:
            mark affected temporal metrics unavailable with reasons
        else:
            run the prespecified paired temporal probe
    finally:
        restore model mode and RNG states
    return {metrics, metric_definitions}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    include measured metrics, definitions, counts and unresolved checks
    request evidence-linked findings and alternative explanations
    distinguish numerical variation, execution defects and behavioral sensitivity
    prohibit inferred intent or unmeasured validation improvement

originality.positive: Integrates execution tracing and direct feature-to-score dependence checks around a concrete GRU4Rec diagnostic inconsistency.
originality.negative: Metamorphic testing, intermediate-tensor comparisons, and controlled input interventions are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Can resolve a blocking ambiguity and provide reliable infrastructure for later recurrent-memory experiments.
future_potential.negative: A successful audit does not itself improve ranking accuracy or establish generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses bounded inference on existing models without fitting additional predictors.
code_difficulty.negative: Intermediate instrumentation and exact agreement with the emitted predictor require careful handling of projections, biases, precision, and padding.

related_work.title: [1] PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Specifies recurrent equations showing why zero inputs need not leave hidden states unchanged.
limitations: Does not establish whether the supplied trained implementation skips padding transitions.

related_work.title: [2] PyTorch numerical accuracy notes
contributions: Explains why batched and individual floating-point computations can differ.
limitations: Does not establish that the observed discrepancies are harmless or justify a particular tolerance.

related_work.title: [3] Model-level metamorphic testing
contributions: The supplied search summary motivates testing equivalent model executions for inconsistencies.
limitations: Does not provide measured findings for this GRU4Rec checkpoint or benchmark.

related_work.title: [4] Heimersheim and Nanda: activation patching guidance
contributions: Motivates complementary restoration and disruption interventions and careful metric selection.
limitations: A GRU4Rec adaptation requires recurrent replay and suitable controls; patching effects do not establish user intent or validation gains.
